title: Audit stream partitioning + SSO-correlation retention governor for RBACv2 admin events
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Admin and RBAC v2 events (role changes, permission grants, SSO config changes) are high-sensitivity, high-cardinality audit rows. Current ingestion stores these in the same primary hot partition as general telemetry which causes spikes in indexing CPU and long-tail query latency during enterprise customer exports. We need an ingestion + storage/retention governor that: separates admin events into dedicated partitions, preserves SSO correlation metadata (SAML assertions / identity provider IDs) for at least 1 year, applies cost-aware indexing and compaction policies, and integrates with RBAC v2 to ensure privileged-event access controls.

Goal: Implement a pipeline and storage policy that guarantees 99.9% availability for audit queries, caps monthly storage spend growth from admin events to <8% of total audit cost, and ensures exports comply with compliance retention requirements (1 year for admin events, 3 years archived cold copy optional).
acceptance_criteria: Admin-event documents are written to a dedicated 'admin' shard namespace separated from 'general' audit streams
SSO/SAML metadata (idp_id, assertion_hash, external_subject_id) is attached and queryable via trace id within 50ms for recent 30 days
Retention policy applied: hot index (30 days) + warm index (11 months) + cold archival (optional object store) configurable per-tenant
Automatic compaction reduces index size for admin events by >=35% without losing required fields for compliance exports
RBAC v2 enforcement: only users with 'audit_admin' or 'security_officer' roles can download or view full SAML assertion fields
Cost guardrail: simulated monthly cost projection for admin-event retention does not exceed 8% growth on our current audit spend baseline
E2E tests and staging runbook exist and verified in staging with synthetic enterprise tenant generating 10k admin events/day
proposed_solution_summary: Add a classifier in the ingest router that tags incoming audit rows as 'admin' when event_type in [role_change, sso_config, permission_grant, service_account_key] OR when sensitivity >= 8. Route 'admin' to a dedicated admin-write pipeline with its own index template: time-based daily indices with smaller refresh interval, stronger compressions (doc_values-only for large arrays), and pre-configured ILM (hot: 30d, warm: 11mo, cold: move to object storage). Persist SSO correlation fields as de-identified but reversible tokens: store assertion_hash and idp_id in index, keep encrypted assertion_blob in KMS-backed blobstore for compliance export workflows. Integrate RBAC v2 check during read/export API endpoints to redact assertion_blob unless caller has audit_admin role. Add autoscaling knobs for admin write pool and set quota per-tenant to avoid noisy-neighbor cost spikes.
monitoring_signals: cpu_indexing_spikes correlated with admin writes reduced by 60% after partitioning
progress_updates: 2025-02-10: Ticket created by Asha. Initial problem statement and goals outlined; requested dependency on ENG-45201 (KMS blobstore encryption work).

2025-02-18: Infra spike: proof-of-concept classifier deployed to staging routing by event_type. Found 12% of general audit flows are mislabelled — classifier threshold updated to include sensitivity score.

2025-02-24: Storage team submitted index template PR with doc_values and ILM policies (PR #1924). Benchmarks show 38% smaller index size on sample admin dataset. Assigned code review to Morgan Rivera.
2025-03-02: Integration tests failing intermittently on export with RBAC v2 mock — root cause: read-path missing role cache refresh. Daniel investigating role cache TTL update.
2025-03-05: Role cache TTL patch merged to staging (PR #7469). Next step: run full 10k events/day staging scenario and validate cost projection model.
blockers: ENG-45201 (KMS-backed blobstore) delayed — until available we cannot store encrypted assertion_blob for exports
Need security review signoff for storing SAML assertion_hash reversible mapping (security review pending)
risk_analysis: Risk: Over-segmentation of indices increases cluster shard count leading to management overhead. Mitigation: use time-based indices with rollover and shard-sizing guidance (target 30–50GB per shard), monitor shard count and use index lifecycle to merge small indices into monthly aggregates for older data. Legal risk: SAML assertion storage must align with data retention contracts; we will add tenant-level opt-in for assertion archival and ensure KMS-backed encryption with per-tenant keys.
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy classifier and admin-write pipeline to staging; 2) Run synthetic traffic for 2 weeks and validate acceptance criteria; 3) Ramp on 3 pilot enterprise tenants with opt-in flag; 4) Gradual rollout to all tenants with tenant quota defaults and opt-in archival; 5) Finalize runbook and retire old export paths after 2 months of stable telemetry.
notes: Avoid storing raw SAML assertions in hot index to limit PII exposure; keep only assertion_hash and idp_id in index
Consider adding a 'sensitivity_score' field computed in authz service to make classifier deterministic
Customer export API should emit audit trail of who accessed the assertion_blob for compliance
